Starting from the notion provided by previous research that the consumers' reference price decreases after exposure to a price promotion (Bambauer-Sachse and Dupuy, 2012, Diamond and Campbell, 1989, Grewal et al., 1998, Lattin and Bucklin, 1989), the first objective of this study is to examine how price promotions with different saving formats (percentage-off vs. amount-off) affect consumers' RP adaptation after one versus several exposures to a price promotion displaying the reduced price and the saving. ... Previous research on repeated exposure to advertising has not considered the saving format in the context of reference price adaptations, but has shown that the number of exposures to price information can explain how consumers react to a price promotion (Kalwani and Yim, 1992, Kalwani et al., 1990, Lattin and Bucklin, 1989) and that an increasing number of exposures changes the way consumers process the price information encountered (Cacioppo and Petty, 1989, Pechmann and Stewart, 1988).
